Not quite yet, and it's an understandable mix-up. During PM Xanana Gusmao's Hanoi visit on 9 June 2026, Vietnam and Timor-Leste signed and exchanged a bilateral agreement for 30-day visa-exempt entry on ordinary passports. But signing isn't the same as being in force: that exemption has not been confirmed as active in official treaty/visa sources, and Timor-Leste is still absent from Vietnam's operative visa-exemption list as of the most recent data (17 August 2026). So for now, Timor-Leste passport holders are NOT visa-free for Vietnam.

What you need today: an e-Visa. It's open to all nationalities (since 15 Aug 2023), covers stays of up to 90 days, costs USD 25 (single-entry) or USD 50 (multiple-entry), takes about 2-3 business days to process, and can be used at any of 83 approved air/land/sea ports of entry. Apply at https://evisa.gov.vn/.

One more requirement either way: your passport needs at least 180 days of validity remaining from your entry date.

Bottom line: don't skip the e-Visa based on that news yet. Before you travel, check https://evisa.gov.vn/ directly to see if the Timor-Leste exemption has since entered into force — if it has, you may be able to skip the e-Visa and enter visa-free for up to 30 days instead.
